Since the state of Him, exalted is He, and the state of them is as has been mentioned, how then could there be any supposition that He would take any of them as a son?

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 19, verse 96:

﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ When the ugly conditions of the disbelievers were detailed, this was followed by mention of the praiseworthy conditions of the believers.

﴿The Most Merciful will bring about for them affection﴾ That is: affection will come to be in their hearts without any effort on their part to seek its causes, apart from their faith and righteous deeds. The mention of the title al-Rahman (the Most Merciful) is because what is promised is among its effects. (p-284) And from the Prophet (ﷺ): "When Allah loves a servant, He says to Jibril (peace be upon him): 'Indeed I love so-and-so, so love him.' So Jibril loves him, then he calls out among the inhabitants of the heaven: 'Indeed Allah loves so-and-so, so love him.' So the inhabitants of the heaven love him, then love is placed for him on the earth."

And the "sin" (in sa-yaj'alu, "will bring about") is for this reason: the surah is Meccan, and they were at that time despised among the disbelievers, so He promised them that, then fulfilled it when Islam grew strong. Or because what is promised is on the Day of Resurrection, when their good deeds are displayed before the witnesses, and He will remove whatever rancor was in their breasts that existed in the world. Perhaps the singling out of this promise from among the noble honors they will be given on the Day of Resurrection is because the disbelievers will on that day fall into mutual hatred, enmity, severance, and mutual cursing.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 19, verse 97:

﴿So We have made it easy⁠ ﴾ That is: the Qur'an.

﴿In your tongue⁠﴾ by sending it down in your language. The "bā'" (ba, "in") here means "ʿalā" (upon). It has also been said that the facilitation (taysīr) is construed with the meaning of sending down (inzāl), i.e., "We have made the Qur'an easy by sending it down in your language." The "fā'" (fa, "so") is for giving the reason for a matter to which the noble composition leads, as if it were said: after the revelation of this noble surah, convey this descended revelation, or give good tidings with it and warn, for We have made it easy only in your clear Arabic tongue.

﴿That you may give good tidings with it to the God-fearing⁠﴾ That is: those who attain taqwa (God-consciousness) by carrying out its commands and prohibitions.

﴿And warn with it a contentious people⁠﴾ who do not believe in it out of obstinacy and stubborn opposition. "Lud" (ludd) is the plural of "alladd," which means one who is very quarrelsome, obstinate and defiant. His, may He be exalted, saying:

And how many generations have We destroyed before them? This is a promise to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), within the threat of destruction against the disbelievers, and an exhortation to him (ﷺ) to warn. That is: We destroyed many generations before these obstinate opponents. His words, exalted is He: ﴿Do you perceive from them anyone, or hear from them a faint sound﴾ are a resumptive clause (isti'naf) that confirms the content of what precedes it. That is: do you perceive any one of them, or see them, or hear from them ﴿a faint sound﴾ (ركزا, rikzan), meaning a hidden voice. The root meaning of rikz is concealment, from which comes rakaza al-rumh (ركز الرمح), when he buried its tip in the ground, and rikaz (ركاز), which is buried, hidden wealth. The meaning is: We destroyed them completely and uprooted them so thoroughly that not one of them is seen, and no hidden sound is heard from them.

From the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surat Maryam will be given ten good deeds for each person who denied Zakariyya and affirmed him, and Yahya, and Isa, and Maryam, and all the prophets mentioned in it, and for each person who called upon Allah the Exalted in this world, and for each person who did not call upon Allah the Exalted."
